newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil fails to recover losses.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil fails to recover losses.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were steady late afternoon on Wednesday in quiet trade as the market failed to recover any of its early day losses, traders said.
"The market is drifting and there are some sellers at the current level," one broker said.
The presence of sellers at the lower levels, about 50 cents below Tuesday's prices, is expected to keep prices down, they said.
The front month January was last quoted at $31.50/$31.70 per barrel, down from Tuesday's $32.05/$32.20. It traded in the afternoon at $31.60 a barrel.
February gas oil traded in the morning at $30.90 and at $31.80 a barrel in the afternoon. The market was last quoted at $30.80/$30.85, against Tuesday's $31.30/$31.45, brokers said.
The market opened sharply lower after the release of bearish U.S. distillate stock data by the American Petroleum Institute (API), brokers said.
On Tuesday, the API data showed that distillate stocks -- diesel and heating oil -- had risen by 2.94 million barrels to nearly 127 million barrels.
As a result, heating oil lost 1.20 cents per gallon to last trade at 71.95 cents on the after hours ACCESS trading system.
January gas oil on London's International Petroleum Exchange opened on Wednesday down 1.50 a tonne at $228.00.

Traders said Asian gas oil fundamentals are unchanged with the recent large Chinese purchases more than covered by regional and Middle East supplies including record exports from South Korea for December.

The Singapore physical gas oil market is being supported by prompt buying interest from a local trader who over the past two days bought two 185,000-barrel cargoes for loading in late January at $32.10 and $32.15 a barrel free-on-board Singapore.
Naphtha swaps were quoted steady from Tuesday with January notionally pegged at $25.30/$25.70 a barrel, one broker said.
Fuel oil was unchanged in quiet trading with January quoted at $120.50/$122.00 per tonne.
